description: A single-panel bibliometric line chart (two curves, no micrographs or spectra) showing Scopus search-result counts by year for two research topics. The x-axis is labelled "Search year" with annual ticks from 2010 to 2022; the y-axis is labelled "Search results, thousands" on a linear scale from 5 to 50 in steps of 5, over a background banded from pale blue at the top to pale yellow at the bottom, with a vertical gridline at every year. Two smooth, monotonically rising curves are plotted and identified by the legend at top left: a blue line labelled "Light-weight steel" and a green line labelled "Fe-Mn-Al-C steel". The blue curve begins just above the 10-thousand level in 2010, passes the 20 level near 2014, crosses 30 around 2019 and finishes just below the 50 level in 2022. The green curve begins near, but below, the 10 level in 2010, reaches roughly 15 by 2016 and finishes close to the 30 level in 2022. Neither curve declines in any year, and the vertical gap between them widens after about 2018. The figure demonstrates that publication output on lightweight steels as a whole is consistently larger and grows faster than output on the narrower Fe-Mn-Al-C subclass, whose growth accelerates after 2019. No numeric data labels are printed on the curves.

subfigures.description: One bibliometric line chart: y-axis "Search results, thousands" (5-50, step 5) versus x-axis "Search year" (2010-2022, annual ticks). Legend entries: blue = "Light-weight steel", green = "Fe-Mn-Al-C steel". Both curves rise monotonically; blue runs from just above 10 (2010) to just under 50 (2022), green from below 10 (2010) to about 30 (2022), with the gap widening after 2018.

observations.observation: The figure is a single line chart with two curves, one blue and one green, plotted against "Search year" on the x-axis (2010 to 2022) and "Search results, thousands" on the y-axis (5 to 50, tick step 5).
The legend contains exactly two entries: "Light-weight steel" (blue line) and "Fe-Mn-Al-C steel" (green line).
The blue "Light-weight steel" curve starts just above the 10-thousand gridline in 2010 and ends just below the 50-thousand gridline in 2022, rising in every year shown.
The green "Fe-Mn-Al-C steel" curve lies below the blue curve for every year and ends near the 30-thousand level in 2022.
The vertical separation between the blue and green curves is small in 2010 and widens substantially towards 2022, indicating faster growth of the broader "Light-weight steel" topic.
No numeric data labels are printed on either curve; values can only be read against the 5, 10, 15, ... 50 gridlines.
The caption states the plot gives the number of publications by research topic from 2010 to 2022 according to the Scopus bibliometric database.

The caption describes the y-axis quantity as publication counts, whereas the axis label itself reads "Search results, thousands", i.e. the plotted values are Scopus search hits scaled in thousands (caption is not legible in the pixels and the axis label is what is visible).

The citing text states that Fe-Mn-Al-C steels are about 18% lighter than conventional steels and show 400 MPa <= ultimate strength <= 1000 MPa, 600 MPa <= ultimate tensile strength <= 2000 MPa and 30% <= total elongation <= 100%.
The citing text attributes the properties of these steels to strengthening mechanisms operating through phase transformations, twinning, or microband formation during deformation.
The citing text describes this material class as high-entropy iron-based alloys with a multiphase structure; none of the panels in this figure address microstructure or mechanical properties.
